# MM-P1-L4-HT03 - Maintenance manual - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HT03

Scope
This document defines the preventative maintenance, calibration, and verification tasks required to maintain the Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3, identified as EQ-P1-L4-HT03, in a condition that ensures process control and product conformance. The scope covers austenitizing controls, thermocouple calibration, control loop checks, door seals, atmosphere control verification, and recordkeeping required by plant quality and safety programs. Related documents include ECN-2026-002, SB-1006, and SOP-P1-L4-02 and must be consulted for change notices, safety bulletins, and operating procedures.

Background and rationale
The furnace is used for critical heat treat cycles where core microstructure and mechanical properties are sensitive to temperature uniformity and setpoint accuracy. The austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 880 °C. Maintaining accurate temperature measurement and control at this setpoint is essential to avoid under- or over-austenitizing, which can lead to nonconforming forgings. Thermocouple drift and control loop degradation are the most common sources of process deviation; therefore, a dedicated calibration and verification regimen is required. The thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 95 days.

Tools and materials
- Calibrated reference temperature source appropriate for high-temperature thermocouple checks (refer to SB-1006 for equipment approval).  
- Portable thermocouple calibrator and cold-junction reference.  
- Replacement thermocouple elements and connectors approved for use in EQ-P1-L4-HT03.  
- Door seal inspection kit and approved gasketing materials.  
- Logbooks, electronic maintenance entry device, or CMMS entry template per SOP-P1-L4-02.  
- Personal protective equipment as required by ECN-2026-002 and plant safety rules.

Procedure
Prepare
- Review applicable process setpoints and recent furnace run history in the electronic records system. Cross-reference any recent engineering changes per ECN-2026-002 before starting work.  
- Notify production and quality leads of planned maintenance and obtain furnace lockout/tagout in accordance with plant safety procedures referenced in SB-1006. Ensure all personnel are trained per SOP-P1-L4-02.

Thermocouple verification and calibration
- Verify the last calibration record in the CMMS or logbook. If the interval since last calibration exceeds the allowed interval, schedule calibration. The thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 95 days.  
- Remove the thermocouple probe following manufacturer handling procedures. Inspect the probe for mechanical damage, insulation breakdown, or contamination. Replace if any defect is found.  
- Perform a two-point check using a calibrated reference source and ambient reference. Document offsets and calculate correction factors. Record raw readings and corrected values in the calibration record.  
- Reinstall the thermocouple in the original sensing location. Verify the cold-junction compensation is set and that connector types match control panel inputs.

Control setpoint and loop check
- With the furnace empty and at a safe state, bring the control system up and confirm the austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 880 °C in the controller configuration. Confirm that the setpoint stored in the controller matches the shop floor operating sheet.  
- Execute a control loop exercise to observe controller response to setpoint changes and confirm that output signals actuate the heating elements or power control devices correctly. Document any asymmetric response or oscillation. Note: do not alter PID parameters without engineering approval per ECN-2026-002.

Mechanical checks and atmosphere verification
- Inspect door seals and gasketing for integrity. Replace degraded seals and document material batch per the parts log. Check door latching hardware for smooth engagement.  
- Verify atmosphere feed and exhaust paths for obstructions. If furnace uses controlled atmosphere, confirm oxygen sensor signals are within expected ranges relative to recorded history. If any deviation exists, tag the furnace out and escalate.

Example corrective action scenarios
- If thermocouple offset exceeds acceptable tolerance documented in SB-1006, replace the thermocouple element and re-run calibration. Record reason for replacement and serial of replacement part.  
- If door seal condition results in measurable heat loss during a verification cycle, replace seal and document energy loss comparison before and after replacement as evidence of correction.

Records to keep
- Calibration certificate for thermocouple including raw readings, correction factors, technician name, and reference equipment identifier. File per SOP-P1-L4-02.  
- Maintenance activity log entry detailing tasks performed, observations, parts replaced, and any process deviations. Include operator and supervisor signoff.  
- Control configuration snapshot showing setpoint and controller model data. Attach any ECN-2026-002 references if configuration differs from baseline.  
- Safety and lockout documentation per SB-1006.

Acceptance criteria
The furnace shall be returned to service only when all of the following conditions are met:
- Thermocouple calibration records show readings within acceptable limits after correction, and the thermocouple is reinstalled with connectors secured.  
- Controller setpoint for austenitizing is confirmed at 880 °C and matches the documented operating sheet used in production.  
- No mechanical defects remain that could compromise temperature uniformity or furnace sealing.  
- All records described above are completed, reviewed, and filed in the CMMS per SOP-P1-L4-02, and the maintenance entry is signed by the responsible technician and reviewer.

Notes and references
- Follow ECN-2026-002 for engineering change implementation.  
- Consult SB-1006 for approved safety devices and PPE requirements.  
- Use SOP-P1-L4-02 for CMMS and recordkeeping workflows.
